newsitem.title: UK: Ex-UK finance minister Lawson stars in TV ads for PEPs.
newsitem.headline: Ex-UK finance minister Lawson stars in TV ads for PEPs.

text.p: Nigel Lawson, Britain's former finance minister who introduced Personal Equity Plans (PEPS), will star in a television commercial for the tax-free investment.
M&G Group, the Britain's largest provider of PEPS, on Wednesday said it will launch an advertising campaign beginning on Monday starring Lawson.

The ad campaign, which will feature Lawson in two 30-second TV commercials, will mark Lawson's advertising debut as well as marking M&G's first television ad campaign. Lawson, who served as chancellor of the exchequer under former Conservative Prime Minister, introduced PEPS in 1986.
M&G declined to say how much Lawson was being paid.

The two million pound ($3.2 million) advertising campaign is designed to strengthen M&G's position as the UK's leading provider of PEPS and raise the fund's awareness with younger investors. Since their introduction, PEPS have attracted 33 billion pounds from private investors.

"M&G has been going for about 70 years," said Rachel Medill, head of corporate communications. "Our name awareness among 50-plus investors is very high. But when you look at the 35- to 45-year-old market we're much less well known.
"We're interested in raising our awareness with that audience," she added.
M&G hopes that by attracting younger investors to PEPS now, it will continue to attract their business as they mature and begin to invest in pension funds, Medill said.
If the ad campaign is successful, M&G may do more television ads in the future, she said.
The idea for using Lawson in the ads was conceived by M&G's ad agency, Rainey Kelly Campbell Roalfe, which approached the former chancellor.
In one ad, Lawson is showed sitting at a table in a vast, marble-walled room. "There are plenty of ways you can invest your money," Lawson says, "...if you really know the ropes."

Lawson watches a television showing news footage of him in his days as chancellor of the exchequer. "But when I created the PEP, I created something that anyone can invest it, without paying a penny in tax to the chancellor."
A voiceover notes, "If you'd invested in an M&G PEP five years ago, by now you could have doubled your money. And that's tax free."
As the camera focuses in on Lawson, he adds, "I must have been in a generous mood."

The second ad plays on Lawson's successful weight loss from his burlier days as chancellor. "There are few certainties in life," says Lawson. "Who'd have predicted the new-shape me? But one thing you can be sure of is you don't have to pay tax on your investment. ...I made sure of that when I created the PEP."
A voiceover notes an investment five years ago in an M&G PEP would have resulted in an average annual return of 16.9 percent, tax-free.
